So, I was in Amsterdam. I forgot to write about it at the time, but I was there for almost two weeks in September, and it was a nice little break from Istanbul and some mess that was going on here. But I didn't go there for tourism or conferences, since I had back from Brazil with a small break in Baltimore in the middle, and I was supposed to be in Istanbul starting my semester here.

So this small detour was mostly to get some work done, deal with some visa things, and to meet a few people I had been meaning to meet for a while. It was also a nice opportunity to see a bit of the city, and to enjoy the Dutch weather, which is quite different from Istanbul's.

During these days there I had the opportunity to talk with some professor about my research, and to get some feedback on a few things I had been working on. It was also a good chance to discuss some potential collaborations. Also, since I am part of this BeyondTheEdge project, I had the chance to meet some of the other researchers involved in the project, specially the other PhDs, so we had some good food and drinks a couple times. 

So I think I don't have much to say about these days in Amsterdam, I basically saw friends, discussed work, cycled a lot around the city (thanks Fernando for the bike!), and went for the bouldering gym just one time, which is a big bummer. Let's see if I will go back in the near future, since I have a proper secondment to do there in a few months.

I will try to post more often and think better about what I want to write here, but usually I just start to write and see where it goes. Anyway, thanks for the attention!
